title: Job 10: Job Pleads With His Maker
body:
Read the chapter → [Job 10](/bible/job/10)

Job speaks in the bitterness of his soul and turns his complaint directly toward the Most High, asking why the one who fashioned him is now destroying him. He reasons that the Most High does not have eyes of flesh, does not see as man sees, and knows Job is not wicked, yet Job is afflicted. He recalls being made as clay, poured out as milk, clothed with skin and flesh and fenced with bones and sinews, and he laments that it would have been better to go from the womb straight to the grave.

**[Job 10:1-4](/bible/job/10#v1)**

> <sup>[1](/bible/job/10#v1)</sup> My soul is weary of my life; I will leave my complaint upon myself; I will speak in the bitterness of my soul.
>
> <sup>[2](/bible/job/10#v2)</sup> I will say unto God, Do not condemn me; shew me wherefore thou contendest with me.
>
> <sup>[3](/bible/job/10#v3)</sup> Is it good unto thee that thou shouldest oppress, that thou shouldest despise the work of thine hands, and shine upon the counsel of the wicked?
>
> <sup>[4](/bible/job/10#v4)</sup> Hast thou eyes of flesh? or seest thou as man seeth?

- Job's soul is weary of his life; he will leave his complaint upon himself and speak in the bitterness of his soul.
- He asks the Most High not to condemn him but to show him why he contendeth with him.
- Is it good to the Most High that he should oppress and despise the work of his own hands and shine upon the counsel of the wicked?
- Does the Most High have eyes of flesh, or does he see as man sees? This is how Job is answering God.

**[Job 10:5-9](/bible/job/10#v5)**

> <sup>[5](/bible/job/10#v5)</sup> Are thy days as the days of man? are thy years as man’s days,
>
> <sup>[6](/bible/job/10#v6)</sup> That thou enquirest after mine iniquity, and searchest after my sin?
>
> <sup>[7](/bible/job/10#v7)</sup> Thou knowest that I am not wicked; and there is none that can deliver out of thine hand.
>
> <sup>[8](/bible/job/10#v8)</sup> Thine hands have made me and fashioned me together round about; yet thou dost destroy me.
>
> <sup>[9](/bible/job/10#v9)</sup> Remember, I beseech thee, that thou hast made me as the clay; and wilt thou bring me into dust again?

- Are the Most High's days as the days of man, and his years as man's days, that he inquireth after Job's iniquity and searcheth after his sin?
- The Most High knows that Job is not wicked, and there is none that can deliver out of his hand.
- His hands have made and fashioned Job together round about, yet he destroys him; Job did not steal anything, he loves his wife and kids, yet he is broken down.
- Job asks the Most High to remember that he made him as the clay and asks whether he will bring him into dust again.

**[Job 10:10-13](/bible/job/10#v10)**

> <sup>[10](/bible/job/10#v10)</sup> Hast thou not poured me out as milk, and curdled me like cheese?
>
> <sup>[11](/bible/job/10#v11)</sup> Thou hast clothed me with skin and flesh, and hast fenced me with bones and sinews.
>
> <sup>[12](/bible/job/10#v12)</sup> Thou hast granted me life and favour, and thy visitation hath preserved my spirit.
>
> <sup>[13](/bible/job/10#v13)</sup> And these things hast thou hid in thine heart: I know that this is with thee.

- The Most High poured Job out as milk and curdled him like cheese.
- He clothed Job with skin and flesh and fenced him with bones and sinews; this is why abortion is a sin, because when a baby is in the womb he is fashioned and brought together by the Most High.
- The bones and sinews are the fence, the foundation that supports the flesh and the skin; a big bang cannot give you skin and flesh fenced with bones and sinews, so that scientific stuff you have to drop and let go.
- The Most High granted Job life and favor, and his visitation preserved his spirit; these things he hid in his heart, and Job knows this is with him.

**[Job 10:14-19](/bible/job/10#v14)**

> <sup>[14](/bible/job/10#v14)</sup> If I sin, then thou markest me, and thou wilt not acquit me from mine iniquity.
>
> <sup>[15](/bible/job/10#v15)</sup> If I be wicked, woe unto me; and if I be righteous, yet will I not lift up my head. I am full of confusion; therefore see thou mine affliction;
>
> <sup>[16](/bible/job/10#v16)</sup> For it increaseth. Thou huntest me as a fierce lion: and again thou shewest thyself marvellous upon me.
>
> <sup>[17](/bible/job/10#v17)</sup> Thou renewest thy witnesses against me, and increasest thine indignation upon me; changes and war are against me.
>
> <sup>[18](/bible/job/10#v18)</sup> Wherefore then hast thou brought me forth out of the womb? Oh that I had given up the ghost, and no eye had seen me!
>
> <sup>[19](/bible/job/10#v19)</sup> I should have been as though I had not been; I should have been carried from the womb to the grave.

- If Job sins, the Most High marks him and will not acquit him of his iniquity.
- If Job be wicked, woe unto him; and if he be righteous, yet will he not lift up his head, for he is full of confusion.
- The Most High hunteth him as a fierce lion, showeth himself marvelous upon him, reneweth his witnesses against him, and increaseth his indignation; changes and war are against Job.
- Job asks why the Most High brought him out of the womb, wishing he had given up the ghost with no eye seeing him.
- Remembering all Job lost, the Sabeans took his substance, his children were killed, the storm fell and killed them, his wife acts out, his friends question him, and he is cursed in his skin from the top of his head to the sole of his feet, boils popping and pussing that he cannot scratch off or bathe clean.
- Job says he should have been as though he had not been, carried from the womb to the grave, because it would have been better to be a stillborn than to endure this.

**[Job 10:20-22](/bible/job/10#v20)**

> <sup>[20](/bible/job/10#v20)</sup> Are not my days few? cease then, and let me alone, that I may take comfort a little,
>
> <sup>[21](/bible/job/10#v21)</sup> Before I go whence I shall not return, even to the land of darkness and the shadow of death;
>
> <sup>[22](/bible/job/10#v22)</sup> A land of darkness, as darkness itself; and of the shadow of death, without any order, and where the light is as darkness.

- Are not Job's days few? He asks the Most High to cease and let him alone that he may take a little comfort before he goes.
- He goes to the place he shall not return from, the land of darkness and the shadow of death, a land of darkness as darkness itself, without any order, where the light is as darkness.
- The land of darkness that is darkness itself is the grave; Job is saying just let him die and go to the grave.
- This also correlates to the shadow of death being America, the land of dry bones; America is the shadow of death to the blacks, Hispanics, and Native Americans, and there is no order here.
- Where the light is as darkness, they take the commandments, statutes, laws, marriage, and congregating together as a cult, as darkness, and they take darkness for light, calling homosexuality, pedophilia, and zoonosis good, which the Most High hates. This is the place without order, the valley of dry bones, the great Babylon.
